concerns.text: T019 mandates blocking submission if '< 8 ratings are present'. The Spec (US1) and Plan define exactly 4 stimuli (Professional, Minimalist, Low-Quality, Neutral). With 2 ratings per stimulus (Credibility, Professionalism), the maximum possible ratings per participant is 8. A threshold of '< 8' implies a requirement for >8 ratings (impossible) or a logic error where 8 is not accepted. This silently weakens the FR to an impossible state or contradicts the experimental design.

T011a creates a consent template with a placeholder `<<INSERT_IRB_APPROVED_TEXT_HERE>>`. T011e describes a manual step to replace this. Constitution Principle VI (Participant Ethics) mandates that 'All human-subject data must be collected under an approved... protocol' and 'Informed consent must be obtained'. A task list that relies on a manual, unverified administrative step to prevent the system from running with a placeholder (T011d only checks for the placeholder in dev mode) creates a semantic gap: the system can technically run in production if the manual step is skipped, violating the constitutional requirement for mandatory IRB compliance before data collection.

T022d (write demographics to CSV) and T022g (CSV export logic) are marked as unchecked (incomplete). The Spec (US1) requires 'Demographic data (Age, Education) is collected' and 'Data is exported to CSV'. Without these tasks, the deliverable for US1 is incomplete, failing to satisfy the acceptance criteria for data collection and export. This is a silent weakening of the FR.

T028d duplicates the logic of T022h (post-hoc duplicate detection). T022h is in Phase 4 (US1) and T028d is in Phase 5 (US2). While duplication isn't a weakening, T028d is marked unchecked while T022h is also unchecked. The acceptance criteria for US1 (Data export with hashed IP) and US2 (Analysis on clean data) both depend on this logic. The fragmentation and lack of completion in both tasks means the 'Data Hygiene' (Constitution Principle III) requirement for valid, deduplicated data is not preserved in the task deliverables.

T047 proposes investigating Redis/SQLite for session persistence. The Plan explicitly constrains the target platform to 'GitHub Actions Free Tier' and 'Browser-based client' with no mention of external DB infrastructure. This task introduces a scope change (paid models/external infrastructure) that is not authorized by the Plan or Spec, violating the 'No silent constitution drift' principle regarding infrastructure constraints.
